{{c|''Againe in the Temple (ab{{ls}}oluing an aduoutre{{ls}}{{ls}}e after his merciful maner, and yet vvithal declaring again{{ls}}t his enemies that he is not a fauourer of {{ls}}inne, no more then Moy{{ls}}es) 12 he teacheth openly, and is not for al that apprehended. telling them both of his Godhead, 21 and of their reprobation, 28 of his exaltation al{{ls}}o by their Crucifying of him. 31 exhorting the beleeuers to per{{ls}}euére: 33 and {{ls}}hewing them that {{ls}}eeke his death, that they are neither free, 39 nor of Abraham, 41 nor of God, 44 but of the Diuel. 45 but that him {{ls}}elfe is of God, 52 and greater and auncienter then Abraham. 59 For the which they goe about to {{ls}}tone him, but in vaine.''}}

{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=8|verse=1}}}}{{sc|Nd}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpō Saturday the 3 Weeke of Lent.}}{{sc|Iesvs}} vvent into the Mount-oliuet: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=2}} and early in the morning againe he came into the temple, and the people came to him, and {{ls}}itting he taught them. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=3}} And the Scribes and Phari{{ls}}ees bring a vvoman taken in aduoutrie: and they did {{ls}}et her in the middes, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=4}} and {{ls}}aid to him, Mai{{ls}}ter, this vvoman vvas euen novv taken in aduoutrie. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=5}} And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 20, 10.''}}* in the lavv Moy{{ls}}es commaunded vs to {{ls}}tone {{ls}}uch. What {{ls}}aie{{ls}}t thou therfore? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=6}} And this they {{ls}}aid tempting him: that they might accu{{ls}}e him. But {{sc|Iesvs}} bovving him {{ls}}elf dovvne, vvith his finger vvrote in the earth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=7}} VVhen they therfore continued a{{ls}}king him: he lifted vp him {{ls}}elf, and {{ls}}aid to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We can not conueniently reprehend or condemne other mens faults, if our {{ls}}elues be guilty of the {{ls}}ame or other greater. ''Cyril in Io. See Annot. Mt. 7, 1''.}}∷ He that is vvithout {{ls}}inne of you, let him fir{{ls}}t throvv the {{ls}}tone at her. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=8}} And againe bovving him {{ls}}elf, he vvrote in the earth. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=9}} And they hearing, went out one by one, beginning at the {{ls}}eniours: and {{sc|Iesvs}} alone remained, and the vvoman {{ls}}tanding in the middes. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=10}} And {{sc|Iesvs}} lifting vp him {{ls}}elf, {{ls}}aid to her, VVoman, vvhere are they that accu{{ls}}ed thee? hath no man condemned thee? {{verse|chapter=8|verse=11}} VVho {{ls}}aid, No man, Lord. And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Augu{{ls}}tine by this example of our Mai{{ls}}ter proueth that Clergie men {{ls}}pecially {{ls}}hould be giuen much to mercie: and that they ought often, as the cau{{ls}}e and time require, to get pardon of the {{ls}}ecular Magi{{ls}}trates for offenders that be penitent. ''Ep. 54''.}}∷ Neither vvil I condemne thee. Goe, and novv {{ls}}inne no more.⊣

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=12}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Go{{ls}}pel vpon Saturday the 4 weeke in Lent.}}b Againe therfore {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}pake to them, {{ls}}aying, I am the light of the vvorld. he that folovveth me, vvalketh not in darkene{{ls}}{{ls}}e: but {{ls}}hal haue the light of life. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=13}} The Phari{{ls}}ees therfore {{ls}}aid to him, Thou giue{{ls}}t te{{ls}}timonie of thy {{ls}}elf: thy te{{ls}}timonie is not true. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}} {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered, and {{ls}}aid to them, Although I doe giue te{{ls}}timonie of my {{ls}}elf, my te{{ls}}timonie is true: becau{{ls}}e I knovv vvhence I came, & vvhither I goe: but you knovv not whence I come, or whither I goe. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}} You iudge according to the fle{{ls}}h: I doe not iudge any man. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}} And if I doe iudge, my iudgement is true: becau{{ls}}e I am not alone, but I and he that {{ls}}ent me, the Father. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}} And in your lavv it is vvritten, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 17, 6. 19, 15.''}}* the te{{ls}}timonie of tvvo men is true. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}} I am he that giue te{{ls}}timonie of my {{ls}}elf: and he that {{ls}}ent me, the Father, giueth te{{ls}}timonie of me. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}} They {{ls}}aid therfore to him, VVhere is thy father? {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvered, Neither me doe you knovv, nor my Father. If you did knovv me: perhaps you might knovv my Father al{{ls}}o. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}} The{{ls}}e vvordes {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}pake in the Trea{{ls}}urie, teaching in the temple: and no man apprehended him, becau{{ls}}e his houre vvas not yet come.⊣
